title: Thoughts on generating real life images to use in photoshop for textures?
author: Spanner-of-war2014
selftext: So I was wondering if this is something that is seen as a OK thing, I end up shifting through a lot of royalty free images to get a base for what I need for my textures, but I recently tried a few images from ai, simple stuff like rusty wall or wood floor, then take it to photoshop to do my own magic, how acceptable is this in your opinions?

comments.author: redditscraperbot2
comments.body: No matter what you do, someone somewhere will express issues with it. But what you're describing here is so inert even I doubt anyone would care.

replies.author: Spanner-of-war2014
replies.body: Thanks for the reply! Most if not all references images i use end up being drastically changed from there base. On paper I think of it was just using it for aid, most of my textures are taken from real life images, and the ones that I've generated look pretty much the same. I just wondered if it's something that maybe I should avoid, it's been a big help getting my texture work flow going, which means more time spent on other areas.

comments.author: Jolva
comments.body:
Ahh, this has been covered by US copyright. If it's good enough for Uncle Sam it's good enough for me.

Current law says that if you create an image with AI you can't own the copyright to it. You can sell the image but you couldn't prevent other people from selling it. However, if you make meaningful changes to the  image, kinda like what you're describing, then it becomes something you own the copyright over.

The language specifically is, "human editing, modification, selection, arrangement, and other expressive choices."

https://www.copyright.gov/ai/Copyright-and-Artificial-Intelligence-Part-2-Copyrightability-Report.pdf?pubDate=20250918

comments.author: thvaz
comments.body: The only thing you will hurt will be the feelings of antis.

replies.author: gefahr
replies.body: No one will know unless OP makes the mistake of telling them. Photoshop has had generative pattern plugins since I was a kid in the 90s. People used those to generate textures for masks and images all the time. This is no different. No one needs to know you started with an external source.
